A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same two-stage warmup and RLVR framework. All 21 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v3, including their appendices, are readable and support comparison across relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original distillation and RLVR experiments, including benchmark accuracies, training curves, completion lengths, and ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds warmup experiments on OLMo/Llama models and a 1,000-example K&K condition.

M1.justification: The procedure remains K&K reasoning-trace distillation followed by target-domain RLVR using Dr. GRPO. Teacher selection, absence of rejection sampling, and the two-stage training design are retained. Additional backbone and sample-size experiments do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use K&K and s1K for distillation and evaluate mathematical reasoning, code generation, and language understanding through MATH/MATH500, HumanEval+, and MMLU-Pro, including physics and history adaptation. The additions vary model configurations and sample counts within this coverage.

E2.justification: The comparison approaches remain untreated base models, s1K distillation, short-CoT distillation, and direct RLVR. The new OLMo/Llama experiments extend the existing base-versus-warmup comparison to additional backbones.

E3.justification: v3 adds warmup runs on OLMo2-1B, OLMo2-7B, Llama-3.2-3B, and Llama-3.1-8B. Appendix A.4.3 adds a Qwen2.5-3B condition using 1,000 K&K examples instead of 4,500, matching s1K's sample count. Existing splits, metrics, and RLVR settings are retained.

E4.justification: Two substantive checks broaden the supplementary analysis: Appendix A.4.1 tests warmup across two additional model families, while A.4.3 investigates whether benefits persist when K&K's sample count matches s1K. These address model dependence and training-data imbalance. Existing alternative-teacher, learning-rate, short-CoT, and cross-domain analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix A.3 in both versions specifies four sampled completions per question and reporting mean accuracy with standard deviation. The added results follow this practice; no changed seed policy, repeated-training-run count, confidence-interval procedure, or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: v3 adds a substantial block of warmup results for four OLMo/Llama backbones in Table 5, including an OLMo2-1B MMLU-Pro decline from 11.7% to 11.0%. Appendix A.4.3 adds 1,000-example results of 51.8±1.4% on MATH, 35.1±1.2% on HumanEval+, and 32.9±0.3% on MMLU-Pro. Existing warmup and RLVR scores are retained.

T1.justification: The K&K task definition and mathematical content are retained. Neither version introduces formal theoretical analysis, and v3 adds no theorem, proof, derivation, or revised formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal claims about generalizable warmup, efficient low-data adaptation, and preserved cross-domain performance. The additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 discusses concerns about Qwen-specific behavior and interprets the additional model-family results as supporting broader applicability. It explicitly discusses the K&K/s1K sample-count imbalance and identifies unexplained s1K degradation on Qwen2.5-14B as requiring further study. Existing history-task and scalability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses in the acknowledgements that some experiments used NYU Abu Dhabi HPC resources. The software stack, prompts, hyperparameter tables, H100 specifications, reported training times, and code/model/data access links are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kim et al. (2025), Shao et al. (2025), and Morishita et al. (2023, 2024). Section 4.2 now distinguishes transferring self-reflection and self-verification skills from earlier formal-logic corpus approaches. This is a localized extension of the existing positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v3 adds targeted discussion and appendix pointers, introduces two A.4 subsections, and adds acknowledgements. It also updates the affiliation and corresponding-author information.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 5, moves the existing K&K puzzle from appendix Table 2 to main-text Table 1, and adds colored difference annotations to Figure 2. Table captions move below their contents, and appendix figures and tables are redistributed. Existing displays remain largely recognizable.

improvement.justification: The additional model-family tests and sample-matched warmup control address useful gaps in v1's empirical support. The gain is limited: the central RLVR evidence remains unchanged, and the favorable s1K discussion does not reconcile the new matched-size K&K results with their lower reported MATH and HumanEval+ means relative to s1K. Overall, v3 provides stronger scrutiny without substantially revising the paper.
